title: Qt: Cache only recently accessed columns text
description:
Remove MINIMIZE_STRING_COPYING define because the code does not even
compile anymore. Do not cache strings when ensuring rows are colorized
to avoid thrashing cache. Store column data only for last 500 accessed
records to ensure there is upper bound for the cache size.

Fixes #18741

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/9143/diffs?diff_id=560064664&start_sha=f423a7c2d74eb177b4a9c4566ac75938f36ff485)
Should we use a QByteArrayList instead? That might avoid unnecessary encoding conversions.
I think everything is already converted to UTF-8 by `col_fill_in` or `proto_custom_set` (and what they call), so all the encoding conversions are already done?
QStrings (unlike std::strings) are UTF-16, so I suppose the question is where and when we want to switch from our native encoding to Qt's.

The cache should hold whatever type `PacketListRecord::columnString` returns. Cached strings are only computed as a result of miss in `PacketListRecord::columnString` and the result is used immediately (or almost immediately) for all visible columns. The number of not used QString conversions should be rather low, i.e. not visible columns (for which Qt model does not query the column string).
Not sure if we should remove itself from cache (`col_text_cache_.remove(fdata->num);`) or just leave the cache clearing to `PacketListRecord::invalidateAllRecords()`.
When large capture is open, then most of the remove calls here would simply be a waste of time, as only 500 (cache size) can be present in the cache.
Rows are deleted in a loop, therefore it just clearing the cache afterwards seems to be the way to go.

This, for obvious reasons, significantly slows down column sorting. The cache all strings (as we have now) is always going to be significantly faster than any cache only needed rows. I don't know how useful it is to sort captures by column and hence whether it would be acceptable to impose arbitrary limits on how many rows can be sorted (simply refuse to sort if there are more).

Sorting by column can be very useful. While some of the use cases are maybe better addressed with a filter, sorting by sequence number in a capture with out of order or retransmitted packets is useful, for example. 

On the other hand, people do accidentally sort by column and freeze the UI. There's a fairly new preference to disable column sorting for that reason. (!6448). Maybe add a maximum rows to sort limit preference as well?

Perhaps tying the "maximum rows to sort" preference to the size of the QCache would make sense?

Yes, it is only sensible to sort when all rows can be cached - otherwise the extra dissections are going to drive the performance below any acceptable levels. The downside is that even if you set the limit to large number, the rows will be cached only after you start sorting (and not immediately after the second pass like done currently). The 500 default seems low enough to not cause excessive slowdowns though.

How would the message related to limit be phrased? "Increase rows cache to at least %d to sort"?

My inclination is to have the preference message directly reference the sorting limit ("maximum number of visible rows to sort" or something), and have the row cache also automatically increase to match that value. Maybe explain in the tooltip for the preference that it increases the cache size and memory consumption.

Or are you suggesting that if the user tries to sort but there are too many rows (or sorting is disabled), instead of silently not sorting they get a pop-up message about changing the preference settings?

!9222 has a suggested implementation. Could probably get rid of the other preference (since 0 rows means the same thing as false for allowing sorting.) I'm not sure what the correct default number is, but I do think 500 is too low.

> Or are you suggesting that if the user tries to sort but there are too many rows (or sorting is disabled), instead of silently not sorting they get a pop-up message about changing the preference settings?

Not necessarily a pop-up, but rather a status bar error message that the limit is too low.

Ah, yes, a status bar error message is much better, a pop-up is a bad idea.

I'm tinkering around with a draft adding a uint preference for the max rows to sort, which perhaps could even obsolete the disable sorting preference (since 0 would be the same as sorting not allowed.)
